preamble: The voiceless sibilant [s] can become [l] by total assimilation to an adjacent lateral, giving a geminate ll. In the prehistory of Latin, an *ls cluster is thought to have assimilated to ll, as in collum 'neck' from Proto-Italic *kʷolsom, and in Goidelic Celtic Proto-Celtic *koslos 'hazel' became Old Irish coll /kol̪/. Outside such clusters a direct [s] > [l] change is not documented, so the shift is rare and strictly conditioned. Greek dialectal ll from *sl (Lesbian χέλλιοι 'thousand') passed through an *hl stage and is not filed here.

examples.note: The cluster *ls assimilated to ll; the etymology is marked as uncertain in Wiktionary (cf. Proto-Germanic *halsaz 'neck').
The cluster *sl assimilated to a geminate (later fortis) l; Brythonic shows the same *koll, which Welsh later turned into coll /kɔɬ/.
